content:
Enrichment Program Manager

Lowell High School, Class of 2019

How do you feel about being made an officer as a freshman?

I feel really proud that I started volunteering with Heart In Motion early. I’m glad that I joined the internship program while I was an 8th grader because it allowed me to be able to spend more time with HIM. I never expected that I would reach to my current position so quickly. I wrote a letter to my future self last year, in the 8th grade and I told myself that my goal was to become a specialist or a coordinator by the end of 9th grade. I would have never predicted that I would come so far, so fast. Whenever I got a new position, I freaked out from excitement, then I felt a little bit nervous. I was scared of messing up because I wanted everything to be perfect. I would spend a lot of time on my first tasks because I wasn’t quite adjusted, so it was a little more difficult. But very quickly, everything was coming together and I started to feel comfortable because the people in HIM genuinely care about each other and are willing to help. They check up on me and ask how I am doing, both online and in-person. Their personalities are the real reason I stick with HIM. If they just left me on my own and just told me to do work, I would have left. In HIM, that is not the case. There is a big handful of officers who I can ask for help and guidance. Everyone is really accepting and that makes my experience with Leadership worth it. My first time preparing a membership report took about 4 hours, but by the end of the term, it only took 1 hour. Even though I felt nervous and unprepared in the beginning, I had a lot of support and I could eventually do tasks with ease. When people praise me for being an officer and climbing the Leadership ladder so quickly, it makes me feel proud of myself and grateful to everyone who helped me reach to where I am now.

What are your hobbies?

I like to play instruments, listen to K-pop, volunteer, edit videos, talk to people and dance. I just do whatever I can to keep myself busy.

How did Heart In Motion impact your life?

Heart In Motion supplied me with many leadership, job, and life skills. It taught me countless of things. I learned how to use google docs, spreadsheets, excel, and other programs, but that wasn’t just it. Heart In Motion really prepares you in many important fields. I learned to communicate with people from improving my customer service skills at events and working with people online. Many people would say that I’m too “nice” and I give in to others. My program director noticed this and taught me to be more assertive and make people listen to you. She taught me how to lead, how to get others to listen to me, and how to run a division. Heart In Motion exposed me to everything and created countless opportunities. Whenever I was being interviewed for a job or position, I would bring up HIM and mention how I learned to step up, take initiative, manage my time, communicate with others, problem solve, or most importantly, how I grew.

Why did you join Leadership?

I joined leadership because of my sister. I was in the 8th grade and she had recommended me to apply for the internship program. If it wasn’t for her, I would not have even considered to apply for any internship. I would not have volunteered very often and I would not have spent my time at home very productively. This advantage of starting early really benefited me. I hope that other people also start volunteering as soon as possible.

San Jose State University
Class of 2018

How has community service impacted your life?
“I came to America in my junior year of high school, and I had no friends at all. I learned that volunteering can actually help me make friends, and I still keep in touch with the friends I have met. With HIM, I was able to meet people from all over the Bay Area.”

Why do you continue volunteering with HIM now that you are in college?
“HIM has tons of activities and lots of events. Very awesome because they always find new things to do. Plus I can meet up with friends who are still in high school and have fun volunteering together.”

How has your experience been with HIM?
“Pretty awesome! You actually have a job when you volunteer, so it’s not boring, like sitting there for hours and getting your service hours. For instance, at the Gay Pride Parade, we actually walk with them in the parade and I never expected that! “

What are your hobbies?
“I love drawing, painting, designing, studying human anatomy.”

Do you value your other hobbies over volunteering for your community?
“When you help others, and you are happy, then you are helping others and helping yourself. I think that hobbies are personal, but community service is dedicated to the greater good, and you can find joy in volunteering. In the world we live in, everything is interconnected, so there is no way that you can do everything by yourself and not rely on others. That’s why you need to value community service more because you can find happiness and help others find theirs.”

Lowell Class of 2019
Spring 2016 Intern
Why did you join Leadership?

When I first joined leadership, I was still a bit withdrawn from the world, and I didn’t really tend to speak to anyone besides the people I already knew. When I joined HIM in the first place, just as a regular volunteer, I had thought “This is great! I’m having fun volunteering and I’m meeting TONS of new people– people I would never have spoken to otherwise.” A few months later, an officer from the leadership program in HIM asked me if I was interested in learning more about leadership positions and what goes on behind the scenes. To this I thought “Hmm, I can meet more people and also work for the organization I love to volunteer for? That sounds amazing!” and immediately signed up, crossing my fingers and hoping that I’d get in.

How did Heart In Motion impact your life?

The first time I ever volunteered anywhere was at the SF Food Bank with HIM, and I had no idea what to expect. I had almost no friends in Heart in Motion, so I just stayed in the corner by myself. Then some random person just came up to me, whom I now know was Netpheel, and asked me about myself for a Hearts of HIM piece. This loosened me up for what was about to happen–the interacting with other people part of volunteering. We were assigned to sort apples into good or bad boxes. Not hard right? But it was more efficient, we found out, to work with other people, so I was forced to work with two complete strangers.

What is one of your favorite memories or events from HIM?

It seems silly now, how scared I was back then when it came to talking to people, because I now ace oral presentations. I can now do interviews and speak to any stranger with confidence, but public speaking was once one of my biggest phobias. So even though I worked with the two other people,  I didn’t talk to them until halfway through our assignment. However, they eventually broke my shell, and in the end I was laughing with them, feeling amazing. This was my first, best, and most life changing experience in my life. Without the help of HIM and its amazing volunteer opportunities, I would never have gotten over my fear of speaking to strangers, and I wouldn’t be nearly as open as the person I am today.

Why do you think you were chosen for this spotlight?

I think it’s because I meet deadlines and try my hardest whenever I can. I fill out forms with precision and patience. I always take time to finish my tasks, and I make sure to remain as punctual as possible. I take serious note of all the mistakes I make in order to never make them again.

What are your hobbies?

I love to garden, because I love the idea of taking something that seems lifeless and dead and nurturing it into something that blossoms with life and color. It’s also just really calming and soothing to garden for hours, pulling out weeds or pruning plants. In my free time I also like to read, because it always makes me happy when I can just lose myself in worlds and realities that are in reality only a few inches away from my face, but thousands of miles away in my mind.

Executive Council
UC Irvine, Class of 2019

How did Heart In Motion impact your life?

Honestly speaking, Heart in Motion is where I’ve met the most amazing, inspiring people ever as well as the place where I pretty much met all of my best friends. Heart in Motion joins students from all over the Bay Area at volunteer events, and through those events, I’ve really made “friendships which last a lifetime.” None of us really knew each other before meeting in leadership, and we didn’t even go to the same schools, but after working with them at volunteer events and doing leadership tasks together, we’ve built a strong bond between us. Even now after we’ve all graduated and moved on to different colleges throughout the state, we still stay in contact with each other and hang out whenever we can. I want to say that Heart in Motion was really a starting point for me to open up to others and start getting involved.

Why do you continue volunteering with HIM now that you are in college?

Why? Well why not? To me, volunteering was never something I did because “it looks good on college apps” or because it was a requirement to graduate. I continue to volunteer because I genuinely find it fun and because it’s something I am passionate about. I don’t care if I have to wake up at an ungodly hour like 4 AM and do some manual labor like setting up tables and handing out food to runners--okay, maybe I do care a bit since I do enjoy sleeping, but that’s not the point--because all those unpleasant thoughts just disappear when thousands of runners come down the row thanking YOU for being there. Yes, the actual participants cheer for you while you cheer for them, and that’s the kind of amazing environment I get to work in when I volunteer. What’s there to hate?

What are your hobbies?

My life revolves around anime, manga, dramas, and K-pop. Seriously, K-pop and anime is life. I will proudly state that I’ve written essays based on those topics for school and I received very nice scores in response. Anime has also taught me many topics essential to school and helped me pass some classes, so I will deny every person’s attempt at trying to convince me that I’m wasting my time. TV is my greatest teacher and it’s going to stay that way. On a side note, I also enjoy playing the violin, baking desserts, and going on dessert dates with friends.

What is one of your favorite memories or events from HIM?

I don’t know if this is exactly my favorite memory, but it certainly is one which appeals to me the most. Quite a few of the marathons we volunteer at get international runners and well let's say I’ve had the weirdest interactions with those internationals, especially when they don’t really speak English. So usually when I get Chinese internationals, I break out those near nonexistent, broken Chinese speaking skills and work my way through explanations. But one time I got Spanish speakers, and I have absolutely no ability to speak Spanish, so I explained everything with over exaggerated gestures. I had to explain to them how to use the time tag, so I literally lifted my foot up to where they could see it (basically the height of the table in front of me) and show them that the time tag goes on the shoe. It wasn’t awkward at all for those around me ;).

Connie Liu

Enrichment Program Manager

Lowell Class of 2019

What are you hobbies?

My hobbies include writing, reading, drawing, spontaneous sleeping during random times in the day, and listening to single songs for hours on repeat. Writing, reading, and drawing are really effective ways to distract yourself from reality and the problems in your life. You have to power to create and absorb while everything around you is broken and falling apart. Listening to songs on repeat for hours is also an awesome way to relieve stress, and it can either help you get over an obsession with a specific song or burn the melody deeper into your brain.

What is one of your favorite memories or events from HIM?

One of my favorite events with Heart In Motion is the Hot Chocolate Run. It was my first event, and it is still the event that brings back the fondest memories. I can still smell the sweetness in the air and picture myself spelling out my name with chocolatey calligraphy in a tray of warm molten chocolate. I gained a much deeper appreciation for marshmallows, and perfected the best technique to pour molten chocolate neatly into Finisher Mugs without staining the neighboring bananas and wafers. It really made all the volunteers feel like chocolateers, and it’s an experience I’ll never forget.

How did you find out about Leadership?

I actually found out about Leadership when I saw a picture posted on Facebook by one of my classmates who was an intern during the term before me. It was a photo of the internship orientation, and I immediately regretted not being part of it. The interns looked like they were having the time of their lives, and looked like they had finally found somewhere where they belonged. Immediately I started badgering that classmate, who informed me that I could sign up for the next term, which I did the moment the application was released.

What is the most valuable skill you have gained from Leadership?

The most valuable skill I’ve gained from internship is probably the mindset that prompts me to finish assignments the moment they’re assigned and to not procrastinate. Is this a skill? I don’t know, but it’s the most prominent thing I’ve learned from Leadership. I used to always put things off until the last second, which really took a toll on my day and how I finished tasks in general. Learning how to manage my time and finish assignments on time has really helped me both in both Leadership and school.

Why did you join Leadership?

I joined Leadership because it’s everything that I needed coming into Lowell. It not only taught me priceless skills and mindsets, but it also provided a family and community of people that I could rely on to help me through my first year of highschool. The things I had heard from previous interns before I became involved were all interesting and engaging, and I was eager to join a program that would let me give back to the community while molding me into the person I am today.

What was your reaction to jumping from an intern to a Program Manager?

Jumping from an Intern to a Program Manager was definitely not something I was expecting. One moment I was an intern struggling to understand everything and trying to catch up to my fellow interns, and next I'm suddenly a Program Manager, tasked with a whole new load of responsibilities, including overseeing specialists and coordinators who know more about my job than I do. It was definitely a promotion that I was not prepared for, but still an experience that I am grateful for. It opened my eyes and forced me to see things as the way they are, and encourages me to this day to be more assertive. I still make many, many mistakes and drive my superiors crazy, but they were also the ones that put me in this position, and understand that mistakes are just part of the learning process. So I hope that I can be a good Program Manager this term and bring the Enrichment Crew up to its full potential.

Summer '16 Intern

Lowell High School

Class of 2019

How did you hear about Leadership?

I heard about Leadership from Enrichment Program Manager Connie Liu. She posted information about an internship opportunity on Lowell's Class of 2019 Facebook page. I was extremely interested in becoming an intern for Heart in Motion, so I decided to apply.

Why did you join leadership?

I believe I have the qualities to lead others and help make a difference in Heart in Motion. At the Escape from Alcatraz event, I helped ensure the integrity and honesty that this organization, Heart in Motion, represents and is known for.

What's one of your favorite memory from HIM?

My most recent volunteer engagement at the Bag Corral at the Escape from Alcatraz triathlon was my favorite memory from Heart in Motion. My group was tasked with sorting out bags that contained the possessions of the athletes, and organizing the Lost and Found area. I can never forget the satisfaction I saw whenever I retrieved an athlete's bags for them. Words of, "Wow! That was quick!" and "Thanks! I didn't even have to find my bag!" gave me a sense of community and happiness. By participating in volunteer acts such as this, I believe that we can all give back to the San Francisco community which has given us so much.

Why do you think you're chosen for this spotlight?

I was flattered to be chosen for this spotlight. It was a nice surprise, since I wasn't expecting it. I appreciate this recognition, and I believe what I did was in line with Heart in Motion's expectation for integrity.

What's your favorite hobby?

I enjoy taking part in the hobbies of reading, writing, drawing, watching anime, cosplaying, and playing JRPGs. Reading, writing, and drawing allow me to solely direct my concentration on a single thing, which in turn has been shown to increase happiness. As the president of the Anime Club at Lowell, it's pretty evident that I love Japanese culture. Anime and JRPGs are nice ways to pipe down and laugh a bit when you're feeling down or stressed. Cosplaying is a big thing for me. Dressing up and acting are parts of cosplay, which I enjoy very much.

Westmoor

Class of 2017

How has your experience been with HIM?

I really like being in HIM because they are really organized and make sure I don't forget an event I signed up for. I really enjoy going to the HIM events because they are fun and I like meeting new people. Some of the events I enjoyed the most are the Ghirardelli Chocolate Festival event. So many people, so much to do, so many thing to see. My favorite part about HIM are the officers. They’re so friendly and courteous and helpful. They are always helpful when I had a question, and they answer so thoroughly.

When did you start volunteering with Heart In Motion?

I started volunteering for Heart In Motion on September 21, 2014 because I wanted some good experience to put on future school applications. Also because my mother didn’t want me to stay at home all day on weekends. Ever since I started volunteering for Heart In Motion, I have been an active member and have learned so much.

What are your hobbies?

I am a swimmer for my high school swim team, and am in multiple clubs so I don't have time to keep track of everything I need to do in a day.

Enrichment Coordinator

Lowell High School

Class of 2018

What are your hobbies?
I really really love photography and drawing. Whenever I'm stressed out or just down, I would just go look for some drawing or photography accounts and that would usually calm me down. It's really relaxing to draw or just go outside and take photos. There's just something about those two hobbies that really calms me down and makes me happy.  I also love just sitting around and listening to music. I get really get into the mood of the music. I don't mind just wasting a few hours just listening to music. During that time, I also get to reflect over life and think about things, it's like a relax and self-reflection time for me. Music is also kind of my motivation to get things done. I feel like it pushes me to finish tasks and without that music, I tend to get off task easily.

How did you find out about Leadership?
I actually found out about internship through browsing around the Heart in Motion site, which might sound kind of weird and creepy. I was super new to Heart in Motion. I've only been to two events actually and wanted to see what else they had and I saw the internship tab. I looked further into it and it seemed super fun and useful so I planned to apply when the applications opened up in the summer, and I applied! I also saw that my friends were tagged in some of their photos posted on Facebook and it looked super cool.
 

Why did you join Leadership?
Similar to the previous question, I applied because it seemed really fun and exciting. I planned to spend my summer volunteering, but I did not really know where to do it at. Heart in Motion came in and it was a perfect opportunity. Since the applications for internship were also open, I applied for that as well. They provided a simple and easy way for me to sign up for events. They also provided a very useful internship where I learned many useful skills that I am very grateful for.

What is the most valuable skill you have gained from Leadership?

I think one of the most valuable skill I've gained from Leadership is my speaking skills. I know it sounds weird and such, but I feel like Leadership really helped me boost my confidence in speaking and talking. Before I joined leadership, I would be very scared to speak up. It would take a lot of courage for me to present a project in class or just to speak to a customer service over the phone. I would get really nervous. I would always get sweaty palm (I know, gross.) and sometimes even a stomach ache. With all those calling, messaging, and talking to people, I feel like it improved A LOT. I don't mind speaking up now. I feel confident whenever I have to speak up in class. (Just give me like 5 minutes to prepare.) I'm very grateful for this skill that I've gained from Leadership.

Winnie Huang

Summer 2016 Intern

Burton

Class of 2019

What is the most valuable skill you have gained from Leadership?

The most valuable skill I gained from leadership was time management skills. I'm usually really lazy, and never get things done on time or be on time, but Leadership has taught me to stop and drop everything that is not important,(being on my phone, watching YouTube videos, eating etc.) and finish my tasks. It also taught me to be early and not late, such as setting reminders or just remembering.

Why do you think you were chosen for this spotlight?

I was really surprised when I had been chosen for spotlight. I think I was chosen for spotlight because I complete my tasks, do well , and I kept trying and learned from my mistakes.

Why did you join Leadership?

I joined leadership because a friend of mine said I should give it a try. She kept convincing me, giving me good reasons why I should join. When I kept thinking negative thoughts, such as I don't even know how to do this and that. She said it’s okay because we are gonna learn how to do all those things.

What are your favorite hobbies?

My favorite hobbies are playing with my cousin's pet dog, spending my free time hanging out with my friends or relatives. I also love editing pictures a lot on my free time, painting my nails and sometimes watching YouTube videos.

What is one of your favorite memories or events from HIM?

One of my favorite memories was the Nike Women event's Saturday expo . I was assigning runners their bib numbers and someone came up to me and asked me in a really curious tone, "Excuse me ,but how old are you?" and I replied "14" . I forgot what she said after, but she probably thinking I was 10 and wondered why a 10 year old would be volunteering.

Alvie Kam

Volunteer

Burton

Class of 2019

How has community service impacted your life?

Throughout my time of volunteering with HIM and other programs & services, I've learned that nothing beats the pleasure of helping out others. In my mind, the whole point of community service is to assist those who needs more hands to support their doings. In return of helping, you are creating a ripple effect of satisfaction to the connected communities. For example, if you are volunteering at a food pantry for any position, you are contributing to its goal of sending out food to those in need. It doesn't matter if you are the person who is signing people in, or the one who is handing out the food. You are still part of the process of giving functionality to the place to serve its purpose, and that feeling is the greatest.

Why did you start volunteering with HIM?

HIM was the first place I went to when I decided I wanted to start volunteering. My brother was the one who actually introduced it to me and told me all these great things about it. The weird thing is how he has never volunteered for HIM, but he seemed to know the majority of things. I thought that if he knew so much about it, then HIM must be a pretty known thing around school. As it turns out, it is. When I registered for my first event, it was bizarre seeing the amounts of people that were volunteering too. With HIM revolving around clubs throughout SFUSD high schools, online works, and social media, like Facebook, Instagram, and Twitter, it was a growing organization. It all seemed amazing to me, so as of today, I continue to choose to be a part of HIM.

Which events did you enjoy the most? Why?

My enjoyment of events comes from the working in the different work environments that I've never encountered before. These includes marathon expos, prepping for festivals, fairs, etc, and working to serve the needy, such as Glide and Food Bank. I believe that I get the most learning experience from these types of events where I'm interacting with strangers, seeing the behind of scenes, and helping the ones who need it the most. Not only am I learning, it's also fun working chatting besides people that has the same intentions and goals.

What's your favorite part about volunteering with HIM?

Every time I volunteer with HIM, it gives me time to not only help out for a good cause, but to also bond and meet new people. From my experience, I have strengthened many friendships throughout the long hours we get for each event. It gave me a chance to meet so many amazing people, including the fellow volunteers working beside me and the many strangers I've encountered in marathons and other types of events. To also see young peers developing skills that will help themselves out as individuals in the future is very motivational. By just looking at the interns, officers, program managers, or just anyone who is in charge of trying to run HIM smoothly gives me a hint of appreciation towards the organization itself regarding how much time they spend behind the scenes to make it possible for the volunteer opportunities.

Angela Sio

Internship Specialist

Balboa

Class of 2018

What are your hobbies?

I enjoy volunteering with Heart in Motion. I know that all of you that are reading right now are like wow... Of course you would say that when l look at you, you look like you go to every event . President this year I heard ? Well honestly I don't know if I deserve it but I do put my heart into what I do. I may not tell those who are doing wrong at events to stop but I have always believed that if I'm doing something correctly people should do the same. I have always believed that respect is earned. All I do is scream and act crazy but it's to put things at ease. But I know when to stop and so should all those who fool around. Any how off topic but I love love love volunteering. It's my escape.

How did Heart In Motion impact your life?

Without Heart in Motion, I wouldn't have met the most amazing and supportive people. I have break downs and issues that are small compared to other people. I wouldn't be confident. I wouldn't be able to act crazy and be accepted. Middle school wasn't the best. There was a lot of drama. I would be scared out of my mind. I would be just another girl wandering the halls but I met people from Washington, Lincoln, Lowell, SOTA and so many other schools. I joined leadership and made my first sophomore friend from Balboa that was like Senpai. I had a bathroom selfie. I felt a part of a family. Someone actually believes in the abilities I never thought I had.

How did you find out about Leadership?

Ms. Dy and Sean. Ms. Dy was like your Angela. You should join leadership and then get into the details. I was persuaded but was still unsure. Then Sean talked to me and told me "You needs a friend to not be lonely." So I asked Bella.

Why did you join Leadership?

I joined leadership because I was intrigued by what both Ms.Dy and  Sean said.

Why do you think you were chosen for this spotlight?

I am fabulous. Yes little conceited but it's true.

What is one of your favorite memories or events from HIM?

There were so many. Starting April one year. It was a hot nice day for a car wash . it was also the most amazing birthday party despite the fact that nine others soaked her in water and creamed her. Ever since that day, we keep laughing at that video. These girls I've met made me laugh, cry,and scream from both excitement and anger. They are like my sisters. They are everything to me. Without them I will not make it here today to tell you all to take a leap of faith. Be yourself and if people don't love who you are right now, the you is what you think truly are.

What is the most valuable skill you have gained from Leadership?

Love :) Compassion :) Everything that I need to be a leader. I am able to stand up for myself and speak my mind. I am able to rant about my issues and have amazing advice that I don't necessarily always follow.

Yared Beltran

Volunteer

Burton

Class of 2019

How has community service impacted your life?

Community service impacted my life by making  me more  confident and assertive when it comes to interacting with people. I am a very shy and quiet person but when I discover this program I learned to go up to people and actually talk or try to answer questions. I learned very quickly that this was something I wanted to do and I'm always so happy to help someone out whether I'm volunteering or out doing something else and someone needs help. Community service has taught me that not everything will go smoothly so sometimes you will need to be prepared to help or deal with it in some ways.

When did you start volunteering with Heart In Motion?

I started volunteering with Heart In Motion on my second semester of high school as a freshman. I was unable to go to other events that happen during that time because of extracellular activities I had after school or on weekends. Until summer came I went to many events and each event was enjoyable.

Why did you start volunteering with HIM?

I started volunteering with HIM because one of my friends Corie Chen invited me to join and here I am.

What is one of your favorite memories or events from HIM?

Honestly all of the events I went to were my favorites because I just really like to help others especially the marathons. Just watching and handing out medals, water, and food to the people who seem to do what most people deem as impossible just inspire me.

How has your experience been working with HIM?

My experience working with HIM was very professional even if I wasn't. The people in this program have so much patience and work so hard to make sure we have a fun and successful experience with the events we go to. They encourage us to go to as many events as we can and I'm glad to go to almost all of them. I grateful that the officers put time in making post, going to the meeting place earlier then they should, reminding volunteers about many things.

What are your favorite hobbies?

My favorite hobbies are mostly running, drawing, reading, and I guess volunteering if that counts as a hobby. Running is one of my top favorite hobbies because I really like to improve on times and it's quite the stress reliever for me personally. Drawing and reading I barely manage to do anymore but when I do it's really relaxing to just think of creative things to draw and reading has always been my thing to do if I can't run because of an injury. Volunteering has kinda become a daily if there's events available and I would just quickly sign up.

Summer '16 Intern

South San Francisco High School

Class of 2019

What are your hobbies?

I love playing golf, badminton, and basketball. I was on the golf and badminton team last school year. I also like watching the professionals play basketball, golf, and baseball. I am a huge Warriors and Giants fan! I enjoy going to their games and watching the players! Last, but definitely not least, I love eating stadium food!

How did Heart In Motion impact your life?

Heart in Motion has impacted my life in a positive way. I have become a better person, as I am able to help others. The feeling when you are volunteering for a good cause is priceless. It is fun to volunteer, and also meet new people.

How did you find out about Leadership?

I found out about leadership from my friend who did internship last summer. She enjoyed it very much and introduced me to it. She told me how much fun it was so I decided to apply. I could step out of my comfort zone and do something different than I would normally do.

Why did you join Leadership?

I joined leadership because I thought it would be an interesting experience. I wanted to learn more about the processes behind Heart in Motion and help out the best I could. I also thought it would be great to contribute to an organization that benefits such a great cause. During this process, I would not only learn about Heart in Motion, but also life lessons along the way.

Why do you think you were chosen for this spotlight?

I think I was chosen for this Spotlight because of my positive attitude and energy. I try to see the good in situations, and do something about it, as opposed to giving up or getting frustrated. I try to have an upbeat spirit and encourage others during tough times or just overall daily life. Being happy and positive is contagious, so it just takes one person to start spreading the happiness! I also have a hardworking and persevering mindset. I work hard in everything I do.

What is one of your favorite memories or events from HIM?

One of my favorite events from Heart in Motion was the Hot Chocolate Expo. It was my first event, and I went with my friend who introduced me to leadership and her sister. Our job was to pass out goodie bags to the runners, and their smiles were priceless. I knew that I was helping them and they were thankful for that.

What is the most valuable skill you have gained from Leadership?

The most valuable skill I have learned from leadership so far is learning how to fill out an electronic waiver. I didn't know how to fill it out on my phone before, but I figured it out so that I don't need a computer. This might seem like a small skill for others, but it made me immensely happy when I finally figured it out. I hope that one day I will be able to use this skill, and pass it on to others as

Bella Liang
Admin Program Director

Lowell High School
Class of 2018

When did you start volunteering with Heart In Motion?
I started volunteering with Heart in Motion as a freshman. By then, I already had plans on joining Heart in Motion but I have not yet heard about the Leadership program. Although I felt this way, I tried to talk to my mom or tried to take on the role of a home caretaker because I really wanted my mom to be normal again, but there was no sign of appreciation in return whatsoever. I felt that my effort was useless and everything I did was futile. When I first received an invite to join Heart In Motion, it was the first time in awhile that I had the courage to try and help the people around me again. I was ready for more disappointment but at the same time I had no idea what to expect. Next I’d film a video of myself, for all my friends and family to watch, thanking them for the wonderful life I had with them. I want to inspire people to be the best version of themselves everyday and leave the world in a better state than they’d entered it in. There’s only so much one person can do, but if the entire human race works together, the sky’s the limit!

What motivates you the most?

How important do you think It Is to ‘Build Character’?

What is your current HIM position and what are your responsibilities in that position?

I am currently an Internship Junior Coordinator, an Executive Assistant, and the Video Production Team Manager at Heart in Motion. Since I am a Coordinator in the Internship department, I had the option of three different roles: Teacher (teach lessons to interns), Mentor (mentor individual interns), and Trainer (training new junior coordinators on how to do the 3 roles). I ended up choosing the role of teacher because I love teaching, giving presentations, and just helping people learn about Heart In Motion in general. The position of EA does seem quite "exclusive", but I actually got this role by simply asking if I could do more work. If HIM sees that you're excited and dedicated to the organization, they will reward that behavior with leadership/management positions. As an EA, I help out each of the four departments: Internship, Membership, Outreach, Events. It definitely seems quite intimidating at first, however, it gives so many new leadership experiences and responsibilities! Last but not least, being the VP Team Manager has truly been an amazing experience. One thing I love about HIM is how it gives so much room for growth and creativity. Before HIM, editing and making videos has always been something that I loved to do for fun. I never thought it could be used for anything useful. However, after making a training video for HIM and getting great feedback from it, I felt so motivated to make videos for something useful. Then, I had the thought of making a team where people could work together and make these videos. At first I was overwhelmed because over 60 people applied at the start, and I learned how to manage, but also how to ask for help. After creating this team, I've been getting to know my fellow VP team leaders: Catherine Hou, Daena Lim, Ivy Tan, and Jessie Chen. What's great about this team is how it links people from different departments, so everyone is working together. In general, it's been great to teach, help out when needed, and work with people to make amazing videos as a result of HIM's opportunities!

How do you want to be remembered?

What is the most valuable lesson you have learned in your life?

It seems like a waste of such a deep question, however, during these times people need to hear it. Since most of a student's interaction is over zoom, this idea of not knowing who you're talking to other than a name and a choppy voice is absolutely frightening. We never wanted any of this to happen, but it did, and we need to adapt. Thinking about it now, it's just so absurd that people are embarrassed to show their faces. Something so integral to making us who we are. I suppose this was the case even before the pandemic and online school. What is it like to be part of HIM Leadership Crew?

Everyone is always making sure to act professional and considerate (just like a real workplace), but the sense of camaraderie peaks through at many times as well. Because in fact, we are more than just an organization. We are a group of kids who want to work together to create change in our communities and make lasting friendships in the process. That's what it's all about when running an organization, being able to make connections with people in order to get stuff done.

How has HIM affected your life so far?

If HIM hadn't come along I'm not exactly sure what I would be doing right now. I originally joined because I got rejected from another Summer internship, but in many ways, I'm so glad that I was. Sure I haven't been able to volunteer for any charity runs yet due to Covid, however, the leadership program has been unlike any other, in that I can work together with others to complete projects and teach others about our organization in the Internship Department. Overall I’ve always enjoyed finding ways to be creative, lead my own projects, etc., and HIM has really given me a medium for that.

What advice can you offer to those thinking of joining the Leadership Program?

I too was apprehensive about joining HIM at the start. I didn't really understand the credibility/what HIM was. After a lot of deliberation, I ended up joining the Summer 2020 internship term and it was something that I definitely don't regret doing. If you're worried about the time commitment, it really isn't that bad. Honestly, it's just as much as you want to commit. If you are drowning in extracurriculars but you still want to be part of leadership, that's ok! Go to the necessary training sessions, have Workchat notifications on just in case someone needs to reach you (the messaging app we use to communicate), and complete whatever mandatory tasks you have (should not be more than an 1 hour a week, but depends on position). If you have a lot of extra time and really want to commit/go up the rankings, you can also put more thought and effort into your tasks, ask PMs about extra work you can do, and end up reaching titles such as Executive Assistant, Program Manager, or even Assistant/Associate director! If we see that you're putting in the work, you will reap the benefits. If you're confused as to what types of tasks we do, they range from training and mentoring in the Internship Department, to making posts in the Outreach department, to updating members in the Membership department, to planning/organizing events in the Events department! Overall, there's no harm in joining leadership, so sign up today and become a leader!
